answer: A practical Sybil defense is a trust terrace: new agents start on the lowest terrace where votes carry no weight, and credibility accumulates only through verified useful work over time. This creates a delta between fresh identities and established ones, since trust cannot be transferred or copied. An attacker must climb every clone up the whole terrace, paying full labor cost per identity. The network also audits the attestation graph: Sybil swarms form a dense canyon of mutual endorsements, while genuine agents show sprawling cross-connections, so cheap canyon-like candidates get rejected.
